# OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Position [L4].** The KJV gives the conception of Jesus Christ to the Holy Ghost acting on Mary, a virgin, with no human father. Joseph was his legal guardian and the husband of his mother, and he was not the one who begat him. I rest this on three lines of text: the stated source of the conception, Mary's stated virginity, and the text's own handling of Joseph's relation to the child.

---

## 1. The source of the conception is stated

**[L1] Matthew 1:18:** "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1] Matthew 1:20:** "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The preposition in both verses is *ek* (G1537), "out of, from a source." Matthew 1:20 reads *to en autē gennēthen ek pneumatos hagiou*. *Gennēthen* (from G1080 *gennaō*) means "begotten or conceived." The text therefore names the Holy Ghost as the source out of which the child was begotten.

**[L3] Luke 1:35:** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *Dio kai* ("therefore also") makes the Holy Ghost's coming the ground of the child's being called the Son of God. *Episkiazō* (G1982) means "to overshadow." It describes the power of the Highest coming upon Mary.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 name the Holy Ghost as the source (*ek*) of the conception. Luke 1:35 gives the mechanism, which is the Holy Ghost coming upon her and the power of the Highest overshadowing her. Where the text gives a complete account of the cause, no second, human begetter is needed for the child.

---

## 2. Mary was a virgin when the conception took place

**[L1] Luke 1:27:** "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." **[L1] Luke 1:34:** "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (G1097), "to know," is used here of sexual knowledge. Mary says *andra ou ginōskō*, "I know not a man" (present tense). **[L3]** The idiom is established in the KJV: Genesis 4:1, "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain" (Hebrew *yāda'*, H3045, "to know"). **[L3]** Genesis 24:16 defines a virgin in the same terms: "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

**[L1] Isaiah 7:14:** "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." **[L2]** The Hebrew word behind the KJV's "virgin" is *'almāh* (H5959). **[L3]** Matthew 1:23 quotes it as fulfilled: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."

**[L4]** Luke 1:34 shows that Mary's own report was that she had known no man. Luke 1:35 answers that report with the Holy Ghost coming upon her, not with a man. Isaiah 7:14 as quoted in Matthew 1:23 sets "virgin" together with "be with child." Mary's virginity at the conception, together with the stated divine source, leaves no place for a biological human father.

---

## 3. Joseph is not the biological father

**[L1] Matthew 1:19:** "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." **[L2]** *Apolusai* (G630), "to release, send away," is the word behind "put her away." **[L1] Matthew 1:20:** "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."

**[L4]** A husband who knew himself to be the father would have had no cause to be minded to put her away privily. Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph acting on the belief that the child was not his, and Matthew 1:20 resolves his fear by an angel's word that the child "is of the Holy Ghost," not of him.

**[L1] Matthew 1:25:** "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." **[L2]** *Ouk eginōsken* ("he knew her not") is imperfect tense, a continued state, and it carries the same idiom of sexual knowledge. **[L3]** Genesis 4:1 gives the same use.

**[L1] Luke 3:23:** "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." **[L2]** *Enomizeto* (G3543) means "was thought, was reckoned." **[L3]** John 6:42 records what the crowd said: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" **[L4]** Luke 3:23 marks the sonship to Joseph as an opinion held (*enomizeto*). John 6:42 shows who held it, namely the crowd, which is the same crowd the text records as contradicting him over where he came from.

**[L3] Luke 2:48–49:** Mary said, "Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Jesus answered, "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" **[L4]** Mary's words use the ordinary household term (Luke 2:48). Jesus's reply redirects "father" to another (Luke 2:49). Together they show the household usage and the child's own claim standing side by side, which agrees with the supposed sonship of Luke 3:23.

---

## 4. The genealogy's grammar breaks at Joseph

**[L1] Matthew 1:16:** "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** In Matthew 1:2–16 the line runs on the active *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat," from father to son. At 1:16 the verb changes. It reads *ex hēs egennēthē Iēsous*, "out of whom [feminine singular] was born Jesus." The relative pronoun *hēs* is feminine, so it points to Mary and not to Joseph. The verb is passive, so Jesus is the one "born," not "begotten by" Joseph. **[L3]** Matthew 1:18 uses the same root, *genesis* (G1078), for "the birth of Jesus Christ."

**[L4]** Matthew 1:2–16 uses "begat" for each father. At the last link, 1:16, the text puts Joseph as "the husband of Mary" and puts Jesus's birth "of whom" in the feminine. A text that kept the same verb for Joseph here would be making him the father. It does not.

---

## 5. A body prepared, and the woman's seed

**[L1] Hebrews 10:5:** "a body hast thou prepared me." **[L2]** *Katērtisō* (G2675) means "to fit, to prepare." **[L3] Genesis 3:15:** "between thy seed and her seed." **[L2]** *Zera'* (H2233) means "seed." **[L4]** The seed spoken of in Genesis 3:15 is assigned to the woman. Hebrews 10:5 names the body as prepared (*katērtisō*) by God, and it is not said to have come from any man. Both verses fit the conception stated in Luke 1:35.

**Descent from David.** **[L1] Romans 1:3** says Christ was "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." **[L2]** *Sperma* (G4690) means "seed, offspring," and it names descent from David and not a father in the begetting. **[L3]** Luke 1:32 says of the child that "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." **[L4]** Davidic descent is attached to Mary by her own line and by the promise. Romans 1:3 and Luke 1:32 state that descent and do not name any begetter besides the Holy Ghost, so they stand with Luke 1:35.

---

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. The conception is stated to be "of the Holy Ghost" (*ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Ghost"). [L1] Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:20; [L2] *ek* (out of, source) and *gennēthen* (begotten); [L3] Luke 1:35, where the Holy Ghost comes upon her and the power of the Highest overshadows her (*episkiazō*), with "therefore also" naming the ground.
2. Mary was a virgin who had known no man when the conception took place. [L1] Luke 1:34 "seeing I know not a man"; [L2] *ginōskō* (to know, of sexual knowledge) and *'almāh* (H5959, the word behind "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14); [L3] Genesis 4:1, Genesis 24:16, Matthew 1:23.
3. Joseph acted as one who was not the father, and the text calls his sonship a supposition. [L1] Matthew 1:19, Matthew 1:25, Luke 3:23; [L2] *enomizeto* (was supposed) and *ouk eginōsken* (he knew her not); [L3] Matthew 1:20, John 6:42.
4. The genealogy breaks from "begat" at Joseph and puts the birth "of whom" in the feminine. [L1] Matthew 1:16; [L2] *egennēsen* (begat) in 1:2–15 against *ex hēs egennēthē* (out of whom [feminine] was born); [L3] Matthew 1:18 on *genesis* (birth).
5. A body was prepared, and the seed is assigned to the woman, which fits a conception without a human father. [L1] Hebrews 10:5; [L2] *katērtisō* (prepared) and *zera'* (seed); [L3] Genesis 3:15, Luke 1:35.
6. Therefore Christ had no biological father. His conception was of the Holy Ghost in Mary a virgin, and Joseph was not the one who begat him. [L1] Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35; [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* and *ginōskō*; [L3] Matthew 1:16, 1:19, 1:25 and Luke 3:23; [L4] links 1–5 each exhibit two layers, and the text names a source, a virgin and a non-father without naming a human begetter.

[L1] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain... [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]."
